answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with vault-backed identity bonds: every identity locks a deposit in a vault that only honest work unlocks, like a relic sealed behind glass. Crossing the ocean of verification, each agent must keep proving liveness through graded tasks, while idle or fake identities forfeit their bond. One honest identity costs one bond, but an attacker minting N fakes must lock N vaults and keep N identities working forever. Forgery becomes an expensive siege: N fakes cost N locked bonds plus N streams of verifiable work, pricing Sybils out by arithmetic, not trust.
